name: Norway (since 1905)
summary: Norway after it peacefully left its union with Sweden in 1905: occupied by Germany in the Second World War, and rich from North Sea oil since the 1970s.

knownFor.label: Roald Amundsen
knownFor.note: First to reach the South Pole.

knownFor.label: Oil Fund
knownFor.note: One of the world’s largest sovereign wealth funds.

location.value: The western Scandinavian Peninsula, plus Svalbard.

terrain.value: Mountains, fjords and a long, rugged coast.

climate.value: Mild on the coast thanks to the Gulf Stream; cold inland and in the north.

resources.value: Oil and gas from the North Sea, fish, hydropower, timber and minerals.

disasters.value: Avalanches, landslides and, more rarely, floods and storms.

population.value: About 2.3 million in 1905; about 5.5 million today.

urbanisation.value: Oslo, the capital, Bergen and Trondheim are the main cities.

disease.value: Public health is excellent, with universal health care.

migration.value: Many emigrated to America before 1930; immigration since the 1970s.

economicBase.value: Shipping, fishing, then oil and gas from 1971.

tradeRoutes.value: Oil, gas and fish are exported to Europe and beyond.

wealth.value: One of the richest countries per person.

moneyAndTax.value: The krone; oil revenues go into the sovereign wealth fund (Government Pension Fund Global), set up in 1995.

inequality.value: Among the lowest income inequality in the world.

keyRulers.value: Gro Harlem Brundtland, Norway’s first female prime minister.

succession.value: Elections to the Storting (parliament) choose governments; the monarchy is hereditary.

institutions.value: The Storting, the constitution of 1814 and independent courts.

stability.value: Neutral in the First World War; invaded and occupied by Nazi Germany from April 1940 to the end of the war.

eliteConflict.value: Coalition politics, with parties on the left and right sharing power by compromise.

armyAndTech.value: A small army; NATO founding member (1949).

territoryChange.value: None since 1905, apart from Svalbard, which gained Norwegian sovereignty under a treaty signed in 1920.

alliancesRivals.value: NATO; voted twice not to join the EU (1972, 1994).

inventions.value: Leading in electric cars and offshore oil technology.

scienceEducation.value: Free universities and high education levels, with strong research in oceans and energy.

openness.value: Open to trade, though Norwegians voted against EU membership in 1972 and 1994.

communicationTransport.value: Ferries, tunnels and bridges along the fjords; the Bergen Railway (1909).

languageWriting.value: Norwegian, written in two official forms (Bokmål and Nynorsk), and Sámi in the north.

artsArchitecture.value: Edvard Munch’s paintings, Henrik Ibsen’s plays and Edvard Grieg’s music, plus the Oslo Opera House.

socialStructure.value: A large middle class, with a strong welfare state.

sharedIdentity.value: Strong national identity and love of nature.

dailyLife.value: Wooden houses; fish, potatoes, brown cheese.

ideasReligions.value: Peace work (Nobel Peace Prize awarded in Oslo).

colonisation.value: None; Norway held no overseas colonies.

riseSignals.value: The personal union with Sweden (from 1814) ended in 1905.

peakPeriod.value: The oil wealth after the first discoveries in 1969–71, put into a national fund.

declineSignals.value: None major; the main long-term question is how to adapt after oil.

outcome.value: Norway continues as an independent kingdom.
